title: Schedule of Notice Given before Departure on a Cancelled Booking — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
Footnote to the cancellation lines of the Air Ticket Fare Brands tariff. Where a booking is given up, the share at which the flat cancellation penalty of the fare brand held is taken, in settling the penalty owed for one traveller, follows the notice the traveller gave.

The notice the traveller gave is counted in whole days from the day the cancellation was confirmed to the outbound departure date, counting the day of departure and not the day of cancellation.

| Notice the traveller gave | Share at which the flat cancellation penalty is taken in settling the penalty owed for one traveller |
| --- | --- |
| 60 days or more | the early-notice share of 0.55 |
| 15 days or more but fewer than 60 | the advance-notice share of 0.80 |
| fewer than 3 days | the late-notice share of 1.30 |
| any other notice | the flat cancellation penalty is taken in full in settling the penalty owed for one traveller |

Either side of each boundary. A notice of exactly 60 days is a notice of 60 days or more, and the flat cancellation penalty is taken at the early-notice share of 0.55 in settling the penalty owed for one traveller; a notice of 59 days falls in the band of 15 days or more but fewer than 60, and the share is the advance-notice share of 0.80. A notice of exactly 15 days is taken at 0.80; a notice of 14 days is neither 15 days or more nor fewer than 3 days, so the flat cancellation penalty is taken in full in settling the penalty owed for one traveller. A notice of exactly 3 days is not fewer than 3 days, so the flat cancellation penalty is again taken in full in settling that figure; a notice of 2 days is fewer than 3 days, and the flat cancellation penalty is taken at the late-notice share of 1.30.

The counting rule worked on hypothetical dates. Where a cancellation is confirmed on the 1st of a month and the outbound departure date is the 2nd of that same month, the day of departure counts and the day of cancellation does not, so the notice the traveller gave is 1 whole day, which is fewer than 3 days. Where a cancellation is confirmed on the 1st of a month and the outbound departure date is the 16th of that same month, the notice is 15 whole days, which is 15 days or more but fewer than 60.
